Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled app_screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_scroll
entries.description:
Scroll the content at (x, y) in one window of a granted application without bringing it to the front.

dy.description: Vertical scroll amount. Positive scrolls toward the bottom, negative toward the top. Each unit is ~5% of the window's full scroll range (it sets the scrollbar value, not pixels), and the result saturates at the top/bottom — use small values like 2-5 and re-screenshot.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_type
entries.description:
Type text into one window of a granted application without bringing it to the front. Target by coordinate, element_index, or target: 'focused' (writes to the app's currently-focused text element — use this for Pages/Keynote-style apps where the document body is a canvas). Replaces the current selection. Only target TEXT fields: typing at a pop-up button, dropdown, or other non-text control is refused (the text would land in whatever field has keyboard focus instead). One exception: a web page's dropdown can be given an option's text with target: 'focused' once app_focus says it holds keyboard focus.

For the menu bar use app_menu. `app` says which application a call acts on. To act in another granted application, call the app_* tools with that application; no release is needed in between. When you come back to an application, take a fresh app_screenshot first: a coordinate or an element_index points at a place in the capture it came from, not at an element.

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

coordinate.description: (x, y) in pixels of the most recent app_screenshot's full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled app_screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones — the AX summary lines use the same space). (0, 0) is the frame's top-left corner; an app_screenshot of the window is required first. Mutually exclusive with element_index and target.

element_index.description: Index into the AX summary returned by the last app_screenshot (the [N] prefix on each line). Targets that element's center directly instead of by coordinate. Use when coordinate-based clicking returns unsupported(canvas). Refused if something from another page inside the window (an embedded page, or the page around one) is at that position now, or if the action would go to something else of the same page than that element. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and target.

target.description:
Dispatch against the application's currently-focused UI element (AXFocusedUIElement) instead of hit-testing at a coordinate. Use for canvas-heavy apps (Pages, Keynote) where the document body has no positional accessibility elements but the app's own text cursor is somewhere editable. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and element_index.

If you omit ALL of coordinate, element_index, and target, the action defaults to the same point as your most recent app_* action on this window — so [click coord, type text, key combo] chains naturally without repeating the coordinate.

overwrite_existing.description: Without it (and without mode: "replace") app_type REFUSES (unsupported: would_replace_content) to type where that would replace text, so you don't clobber a draft or document: when text is selected in the field, and when positional insert (set AXSelectedText) doesn't work for this app and the field already has content, where the only background fallback is replacing the WHOLE field. A selection or content whose read fails, or that the app counts but does not show, counts as being there. Set true to proceed. In either case this can replace ALL of the field's content; at most the first 500 characters of what was replaced come back in the result, and only if the write can be confirmed, so a longer text cannot be restored from the result.

mode.description: insert (default) writes at the caret/selection. replace writes over all of the field's text in one call — use when you need to overwrite the whole field rather than append. Not for a text box on a Keynote-style canvas: there nothing gets selected first, so old text stays behind; select the box's text first as app_key describes, then insert.

disable_substitutions.description: Disable the app's Text Replacement / autocorrect around this type (so e.g. "backpropagation" is not mangled), then restore the user's prior setting afterward.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every call. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_zoom
entries.description:
Get a closer look at part of a window you have already captured with app_screenshot: returns just that region, at the display's full pixel density so small text and fine detail are legible. Reading aid only — it does not replace your app_screenshot: coordinates for app_click and every other app_* tool keep referring to the app_screenshot, never to the zoomed image, and the zoomed image carries no element summary.

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu. `app` says which application a call acts on. To act in another granted application, call the app_* tools with that application; no release is needed in between. When you come back to an application, take a fresh app_screenshot first: a coordinate or an element_index points at a place in the capture it came from, not at an element.

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

region.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1]: left, top, right, bottom edges of the region, in pixels of the most recent app_screenshot's full-resolution coordinate frame (same space as `coordinate`).

scale.description: Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of actions in ONE tool call. Each individual tool call requires a model→API round trip (seconds); batching a predictable sequence eliminates all but one. Use this whenever you can predict the outcome of several actions ahead — e.g. click a field, type into it, press Return. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call. In this session the tools that each carry out one of this tool's actions (left_click, type, key, scroll, left_click_drag, screenshot, etc.) are not available on their own: a single action is a one-item batch. The app_* tools (app_screenshot, app_click, app_type, app_key, app_batch, etc.) act on granted applications without taking over the screen.

action.description: The action to perform.

coordinate.description: (x, y) for click/mouse_move/scroll/left_click_drag end point.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): Rectangle to zoom into. For zoom only. Coordinate space: the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this batch (never a mid-batch screenshot, never a prior zoom).

scale.description: For screenshot/zoom only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y) drag start — left_click_drag only. Omit to drag from current cursor.

text.description: For type: the text. For key/hold_key: the chord string. For click/scroll: modifier keys to hold.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every action except mouse_move, scroll, screenshot, zoom, cursor_position and wait. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

save_to_disk.description: Save the images produced by any screenshot/zoom actions in this batch to disk so they can be attached to a message for the user. The saved path(s) are returned in the result. Only set this when you intend to share the image(s) — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

Under full-screen control, the app is brought to the front. The target must already be in the session allowlist — call request_access first.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__switch_display
entries.description: Switch which monitor subsequent screenshots capture. Use this when the application you need is on a different monitor than the one shown. The screenshot tool tells you which monitor it captured and lists other attached monitors by name — pass one of those names here. After switching, call screenshot to see the new monitor. display.description: Monitor name from the screenshot note (e.g. "Built-in Retina Display", "LG UltraFine"), or "auto" to re-enable automatic selection.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_batch
entries.description: Queue multiple teach steps in one tool call. Parallels computer_batch: N steps → one model↔API round trip instead of N. Each step still shows a tooltip and waits for the user's Next click, but YOU aren't waiting for a round trip between steps. You can call teach_batch multiple times in one tour — treat each batch as one predictable SEGMENT (typically: all the steps on one page). The returned screenshot shows the state after the batch's final actions; anchor the NEXT teach_batch against it. WITHIN a batch, all anchors and click coordinates refer to the PRE-BATCH screenshot (same invariant as computer_batch) — for steps 2+ in a batch, either omit anchor (centered tooltip) or target elements you know won't have moved. Good pattern: batch 5 tooltips on page A (last step navigates) → read returned screenshot → batch 3 tooltips on page B → done. Returns {exited:true, stepsCompleted:N} if the user clicks Exit — do NOT call again after that; {stepsCompleted, stepFailed, ...} if an action errors mid-batch; otherwise {stepsCompleted, results:[...]} plus a final screenshot. Fall back to individual teach_step calls when you need to react to each intermediate screenshot.

explanation.description: Tooltip body text. Explain what the user is looking at and why it matters. This is the ONLY place the user sees your words — be complete but concise.

next_preview.description: One line describing exactly what will happen when the user clicks Next. Example: "Next: I'll click Create Bucket and type the name." Shown below the explanation in a smaller font.

anchor.description: (x, y) — where the tooltip arrow points. Horizontal pixel position read directly from the most recent screenshot image, measured from the left edge. The server handles all scaling. Omit to center the tooltip with no arrow (for general-context steps).

action.description: The action to perform.

coordinate.description: (x, y) for click/mouse_move/scroll/left_click_drag end point.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): Rectangle to zoom into. For zoom only. Coordinate space: the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this batch (never a mid-batch screenshot, never a prior zoom).

Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y) drag start — left_click_drag only. Omit to drag from current cursor.

text.description: For type: the text. For key/hold_key: the chord string. For click/scroll: modifier keys to hold.

actions.description: Actions to execute when the user clicks Next. Same item schema as computer_batch.actions. Empty array is valid for purely explanatory steps. Actions run sequentially and stop on first error.

steps.description: Ordered steps. Validated upfront — a typo in step 5 errors before any tooltip shows.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_step
entries.description: Show one guided-tour tooltip and wait for the user to click Next. On Next, execute the actions, take a fresh screenshot, and return both — you do NOT need a separate screenshot call between steps. The returned image shows the state after your actions ran; anchor the next teach_step against it. IMPORTANT — the user only sees the tooltip during teach mode. Put ALL narration in `explanation`. Text you emit outside teach_step calls is NOT visible until teach mode ends. Pack as many actions as possible into each step's `actions` array — the user waits through the whole round trip between clicks, so one step that fills a form beats five steps that fill one field each. Returns {exited:true} if the user clicks Exit — do not call teach_step again after that. Take an initial screenshot before your FIRST teach_step to anchor it.

explanation.description: Tooltip body text. Explain what the user is looking at and why it matters. This is the ONLY place the user sees your words — be complete but concise.

next_preview.description: One line describing exactly what will happen when the user clicks Next. Example: "Next: I'll click Create Bucket and type the name." Shown below the explanation in a smaller font.

anchor.description: (x, y) — where the tooltip arrow points. Horizontal pixel position read directly from the most recent screenshot image, measured from the left edge. The server handles all scaling. Omit to center the tooltip with no arrow (for general-context steps).

action.description: The action to perform.

coordinate.description: (x, y) for click/mouse_move/scroll/left_click_drag end point.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): Rectangle to zoom into. For zoom only. Coordinate space: the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this batch (never a mid-batch screenshot, never a prior zoom).

scale.description: For screenshot/zoom only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y) drag start — left_click_drag only. Omit to drag from current cursor.

text.description: For type: the text. For key/hold_key: the chord string. For click/scroll: modifier keys to hold.

actions.description: Actions to execute when the user clicks Next. Same item schema as computer_batch.actions. Empty array is valid for purely explanatory steps. Actions run sequentially and stop on first error.

I gave it its own worktree at `~/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/byoai` and removed my earlier uncommitted edits from the shared `jusprin-newui` checkout. Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed** (all in [Preferences.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx) and [styles.css](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css)):
- **Sidebar:** the BYOAI row is a bit taller than the others so both lines fit. The sidebar stays its usual 208px wide. Screen readers announce the row as "BYOAI, Bring Your Own AI".

- **Account page:** the sentence that points people to their own keys now links to "the BYOAI section".
- **Tests:** four tests that looked for the old "AI" label now look for "BYOAI".

- **Automated:** the type-check and all 692 Agent UI tests pass on the integration branch.
- **Visual:** I rendered the Preferences page with the real components and stylesheet, in light and dark mode, with BYOAI selected and with Account selected. The screenshot I sent shows the BYOAI page.

**Still open:** the BYOAI page still shows the JusPrin sign-up card at the top, as you can see in the screenshot. That clashes with the new name. Removing the card depends on a decision you haven't made yet.

- **Open Account instead (my pick).** A new user lands on the sign-up offer, with the link to bring their own key right below it. Then I can remove the card from BYOAI. The cost is one extra click for people who use their own keys.
- **Keep opening BYOAI.** Then the card has to stay on BYOAI, or new users would never see the sign-up offer.

=== d7975301fd
First launch, Account and wording: the AI name, settings menus, a server-filled Account box, no import Retry

Squashed from jusprin-newui-integration (8acb12318c..976f81a714).

First launch (welcome, sign-up, printer step, OrcaSlicer import result):
- The sign-up offer no longer names a plan: "Good for your first month.
  That's about 100 messages to AI." Where the offer is drawn at rest it
  adds "After that, 50 free credits a month. No card needed."
- "Sign up free" sends the code with the address in one press.
- "Use your own AI account" is a card, not a link.
- The printer step says what skipping means: files are sliced for a 250 mm
  Klipper printer until one is added.
- The import result names the filaments imported, points a filament with a
  missing base at the filament menu, and has no Retry button. An unreadable
  file or a preset that failed to load says to try again from
  File › Import › Import from OrcaSlicer…, which lists the failed items
  again. Removed with the button: onboarding_import_retry, the import
  window's retry action, retry_orca_import, OrcaImporter::retry and the
  "retryable" field.

Preferences › Account:
- Shows a box the JusPrin server fills (GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account_box),
  first used for the launch offer. HTML shows near the top; 204, an error
  or no network shows nothing. It is asked again after sign-in or out and
  when the window gets focus. The HTML runs in a sandboxed iframe with no
  scripts, because wxWidgets puts the app bridge into every frame.

Wording (decisions of 2026-11-06 on the wording-sweep report):
- "AI" everywhere a person reads: the panel, Preferences › AI, Home, print
  issues, calibration prompts and error messages. Text the model reads
  still says "the app".
- "Printer settings…" (Home's printer menu, the main window's printer menu)
  and "Filament settings…" open OrcaSlicer's settings window. A new
  "Ask AI about printer/filament settings…" row under each opens the chat.
- G-code hashes are internal: gone from the print history, its search and
  report form, and the chat's G-code marker.
- No outcome words: Home printer cards say only "last print finished"; a
  print history row for a print nobody saw end is not drawn.
- "never printed" becomes ", never sent to a printer".
- The prefilled GitHub issue (issue_report_open) is offered in Klipper and
  OctoPrint connection chats too, with the host's program in its footer.

OrcaSlicer cloud login: JusPrin stores use_encrypted_token_file as true at
every launch, so other local builds and the restart after installing the
Bambu plug-in no longer ask for the login keychain password. A login kept
only in the keychain appears signed out once.

Docs: agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md, how a screen is designed
and checked (cold-reader check, five wording patterns to avoid); AGENTS.md
and the docs README point to it.

Tested on the integration branch: AgentUI vitest 692, HomeUI vitest 157,
tsc clean in both, jusprin_tests 168 cases, agent_bridge_tests 556 cases.
Shell harness default, printer-menu and print-issues pass; printer-setup
and home-live each fail one check that also fails on the base commit.

 AGENTS.md                                          |   1 +
=== b0a2fe3b08
First launch and File › Import: a clearer sign-up offer, and OrcaSlicer's printers brought in now or later, each one chosen, with one profile reload

Sign-up and the welcome:
- The offer reads "Sign up and get 500 free credits", says they last the
  first month and come to about 100 messages on Expert, and the email
  button reads "Sign up free" with "Already have an account? Sign in"
  beside it. 500 credits for a month and 5 credits an Expert message are
  the gateway's values (JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS and its model aliases,
  checked on staging 2026-11-05).
- The email door asks for a code first; "Use a password instead" reveals
  the password row. The code step says the email can be opened on a phone.
- After signing in, the welcome and the printer step lead with the credits
  ("You got 500 free credits for signing up, good until 5 December."),
  then "Signed in as ...". The sign-up lot is named "Sign-up credits".
- "Use your own AI account instead" replaces the two free-door cards. The
  browser wait reads "Finish in your browser."

First launch, Printers step:
- The OrcaSlicer import screen lists the printers OrcaSlicer has saved and
  the ones its setup wizard ticked, all ticked at first. Only the ticked
  ones are imported (orca_import_chosen), with every filament and process.
  It says which printer JusPrin starts with: the one OrcaSlicer had
  selected when it is ticked. Each saved printer's base profile is
  installed first, so it imports instead of failing on a missing base.
- "Choose my printer instead" opens "Which printer do you have?", a screen
  of its own, which shows "Reading this printer's settings..." while a
  model loads. A printer the person skips shows as "No printer yet", and
  every no-printer line says files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer
  until the person adds theirs.
- The import result lists each failure with its reason as a sentence and
  shows Retry only when some failure can be fixed by retrying
  (orca_import_retryable: an unreadable file, or a preset JusPrin couldn't
  load). Retry keeps the printer the first try selected.

File › Import › Import from OrcaSlicer... (new, after the first launch):
- A window over the current screen finds OrcaSlicer's folder the same
  way, lists its printers with tick boxes and marks the ones JusPrin
  already has as "Already in JusPrin". A preset counts as already there
  when JusPrin has one with the same name and the same base, compared as
  JusPrin loads the base, so a second import brings nothing and saves no
  "(Orca copy)". "Choose another folder..." stays here; the first launch
  no longer offers it.
- It leaves the open project's printer, filaments and process as they
  were; imported printers only join the printer menu (Kenneth,
  2026-11-05).
- MainFrame.cpp (OrcaSlicer-owned) gets one additive append_menu_item
  call in init_menubar_as_editor, in the import_menu block right after
  "Import Configs". It calls JusPrin::installed_shell()->open_orca_import()
  and is enabled only when the shell is installed. Carry it there at
  each rebase.

Shared by both:
- OrcaImporter does the detecting, importing, retrying and folder
  picking. Every vendor, model and nozzle the import needs is installed
  with one PresetBundle::apply_vendor_config
  (SetupCommands::install_printer_profiles), which puts the previous
  setup back if it fails; before, each printer reloaded every preset.
- The printer list and result lines are one component,
  AgentUI/src/components/OrcaImportLists.tsx, with its own stylesheet and
  a guard test that it uses only variables both pages define.

content.text: Shown in the next-step box. Your closing message is your answer to the user: write it now, in full, as the last thing you say this turn. The box asks your question, so do not ask it again.

Yes, the card was still there last round. I'd left it because removing it depended on where the "Set up AI" buttons go. I took your question as a yes and made both changes. The work is on `jusprin-newui-integration` in `~/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/byoai`, and nothing is committed.

## BYOAI without the JusPrin account

**The BYOAI page** no longer shows the JusPrin sign-up or sign-in card (screenshot sent):
- The intro reads: "Bring Your Own AI: an API key or an AI app you already pay for. No JusPrin account needed."
- A line at the bottom says "Rather use JusPrin's own AI? Sign up in Account". It's hidden once you're signed in.
- The privacy note at the bottom covers only your own provider now.

**The Account page** gets the sentence that used to sit on BYOAI: with a JusPrin account, JusPrin receives your messages and passes them to the model provider it uses.

**The "Set up AI" buttons now open Account instead of BYOAI.** Otherwise new users would never see the sign-up offer. This affects:
- the chat's "not set up" pane, its setup bar and the composer's configure link
- the printer chat's "Set up AI" button
- the "Set up" button on print-issue bubbles in the 3D view
- the calibration prompt when no AI is set up

The first-launch "use your own AI account" card still opens BYOAI, since that one is specifically about your own key.

**Testing:**
- The type-check and all 692 Agent UI tests pass. Four of those tests changed to expect Account.
- I rendered both pages with the real stylesheet and checked them by eye.
- **Not run:** the native C++ change (two lines in `ShellController.cpp`) and the three shell-harness checks I updated to expect Account. Running them means building JusPrin from this new worktree, which has no build folder yet.

## The last two commits on `jusprin-newui`

**My recommendation is not to squash them.** They overlap but aren't one task, and squashing would break the shared history.

- **They overlap, but they aren't one task.** `b0a2fe3b08` (Nov 6) is the first launch and the new File › Import from OrcaSlicer window. `d7975301fd` (Nov 7) does revise some of that work. It rewrites the sign-up offer wording and removes the import Retry button that the Nov 6 commit added. The two commits touch 41 of the same files. But most of the Nov 7 commit is unrelated: the server-filled Account box, the app-wide "AI" wording sweep, G-code hashes leaving the print history, the OrcaSlicer cloud-login keychain fix, and the design-guidelines doc.
- **Squashing would rewrite history other branches build on.** `b0a2fe3b08` is already pushed, and `origin/jusprin-newui` points at it. `jusprin-newui-integration` is built on top of it too. Squashing would need a force-push to `jusprin-newui` and would make it diverge from the integration branch. The Nov 7 commit is local only and is itself a squash of integration commits.
- **One combined commit would be about 120 files.** It would carry two long, separate messages, and you could no longer revert the first-launch work apart from the wording sweep.

## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

content.text:
Run these from `~/Projects/JusPrin`.

To see the recent commits on the integration branch:

```bash
git log --oneline -15 jusprin-newui-integration
```

To see only the commits that aren't squashed into `jusprin-newui` yet, start from the last integration commit the squash covered (`976f81a714`):

```bash
git log --oneline 976f81a714..jusprin-newui-integration
```

Don't use `git log jusprin-newui..jusprin-newui-integration` for that question. Because of the squash, git doesn't see those seven commits as shared, so it lists them as missing even though their content is already in `jusprin-newui`.

To confirm the two branches match except for those unsquashed commits (no output means they match up to that point):

```bash
git diff --stat jusprin-newui 976f81a714
```

To see what a single commit changed:

```bash
git show --stat 0f76c3888d
```

To compare your local integration branch with GitHub:

```bash
git fetch origin && git log --oneline origin/jusprin-newui-integration..jusprin-newui-integration
```

After your next squash, swap `976f81a714` for the new last-covered commit. Your squash commit messages already record it, in the "Squashed from jusprin-newui-integration (A..B)" line.
